sections.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
sections.comment: Project website listed on the arXiv abstract page.
sections.abstract: The authors frame agentic robotics as foundation models coordinating skills and tools in a closed loop, and propose an evaluation framework and roadmap toward sustained physical autonomy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose Embodied System 2 (a foundation model plus embodied harness) as the decision-making core, with an evaluation framework distinguishing model capability from closed-loop system performance.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a perspective and synthesis, not a new robot-system experiment; the authors note reviewed benchmark settings differ and some simulations pause while models deliberate, limiting direct comparisons.

sections.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
sections.abstract: The authors describe an agent combining large-scale keyboard-and-mouse pretraining, sparse-reasoning instruction tuning, multi-turn reinforcement learning, memory, and real-time serving, and report competitive performance across selected 3D and 2D games.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine cross-game interaction data and training with a shared perception-memory-reasoning-control pipeline, reporting long-horizon game results and a cloud-edge inference system for real-time play.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say evaluation covers selected environments and task structures; transfer depends on training-data coverage, and the paper identifies lower serving cost and deeper deliberation as remaining issues.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The 2026-11-16 Trending AI Today archive records 36 Hugging Face Daily Papers upvotes at 07:00 UTC; its cross-list spans language, AI, and vision.

sections.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
sections.comment: Work in process; website listed on the arXiv abstract page.
sections.abstract: The authors measure how visual dependence reduces draft-token acceptance, then propose adaptively upweighting visually dependent tokens and using sparse attention for long videos; they report lossless decoding speedups up to 3.58×.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' visually aware diffusion drafter reweights tokens using a visual-dependence measure and adds sparse attention for video; tests cover seven image and three video benchmarks, two VLM sizes, and multiple serving settings.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that long-video drafting remains harder than image drafting; their video approach uses a simple sparse-attention pattern and lightweight fine-tuning rather than a video-specialized drafter.

sections.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL
sections.abstract: The authors introduce HARE, a 1,600-request benchmark for reusing prior SQL, and MEM-SQL, which stores query templates, SQL blocks, and schema mappings; across six language models they report higher execution accuracy with fewer tokens and lower latency than direct generation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a history-aware benchmark and a layered memory method with on-demand schema linking; they report mean execution accuracy rising from 37.1% to 50.0%, alongside reduced input tokens and latency.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report that accuracy drops from 56.7% to 29.7% when several verified queries must be recombined, particularly when reused pieces need a new query structure or shared join.
sections.scope_note: Primary category cs.DB, included because the abstract makes its LLM-based text-to-SQL AI contribution unambiguous.

sections.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
sections.abstract: The authors propose a large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion without a pretrained autoencoder or cascaded stages, reporting quality competitive with latent-diffusion baselines and camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use a simple pixel-space video Transformer and ablate patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization; the abstract reports class-conditioned and unconditional video results plus a camera-conditioned RGB-disparity demonstration.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's evaluation is limited to those generation settings and the camera-conditioned demonstration; it does not establish performance across broader video-generation tasks.
